s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual onset of a bony hard, fixed, and lobulated chest mass in a child
salient_findings: Swelling on the right anterior chest
key_facts: 9-year-old boy
Swelling first appeared as a pea-sized nodule three years earlier
Lesion gradually increased to 0.5 cm in diameter
Lesion remained stable in size
No pain, tenderness, or respiratory symptoms
No other swellings
Mass is non-tender
Overlying skin is normal and freely mobile
Bony outgrowth arising from the lateral aspect of the right sixth rib on radiograph

shortlist.label: Osteochondroma
shortlist.why_kept: Bony outgrowth arising from the rib, consistent with osteochondroma

shortlist.label: Chondroma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cartilaginous origin of the bony hard mass

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bony hard, fixed mass could be an osteoma

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Gradual onset and bony hard mass could be consistent with fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Multiple hereditary exostoses
shortlist.why_kept: Family history not mentioned, but multiple hereditary exostoses could present with a single bony outgrowth

raw.rationale: The presence of a bony outgrowth arising from the lateral aspect of the right sixth rib on radiograph, along with the description of the mass being lobulated, smooth-surfaced, bony hard, and fixed to the underlying rib, is consistent with osteochondroma.

rejected.label: Chondroma
rejected.why: Chondroma typically presents as a cartilaginous tumor, which does not match the bony outgrowth described in the radiograph.

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoma is a benign bone tumor, but it does not typically present as a bony outgrowth from the surface of a bone like osteochondroma.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia is a condition where normal bone is replaced by fibrous tissue, which does not match the description of a bony outgrowth.

rejected.label: Multiple hereditary exostoses
rejected.why: Multiple hereditary exostoses is a condition characterized by multiple osteochondromas, but the vignette only describes a single lesion.
